description: Hi! I'm a Management Information Systems student at Minnesota State University, Mankato, with experience in Python, SQL, Excel, and data visualization. I created Orbit Data Explorers to explore NASA's Earth data and identify environmental trends. I'm looking for teammates interested in data analysis, coding, visualization, or Earth science. Beginners are welcome! I'm excited to collaborate, learn, and build something meaningful together.
summary:
EarthScope is a data analysis and visualization project designed to help users explore environmental changes over time using NASA Earth observation data.

The project aims to make complex environmental information easier to understand through interactive charts and trend analysis. Users will be able to explore changes in selected environmental variables, compare measurements over time, and identify patterns that may indicate environmental change.

Using Python and data visualization tools, EarthScope will examine trends in available Earth science datasets and present findings in a simple, understandable format.

The goal is to help students, researchers, and the public better understand how Earth's environment changes and how data can support informed decisions.
details:
EarthScope is a data analysis and visualization project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge.

Our project explores changes in global temperatures using historical and recent climate datasets. We organized the data into Excel dashboards, charts, and visualizations to help users understand how temperatures change over time.

The project includes historical annual temperature trends from 1880–1929 and recent monthly temperature data from 2025–2026. These datasets allow users to examine patterns across different periods and understand how data visualization can make complex environmental information easier to interpret.

We used Microsoft Excel for data analysis and dashboard development, CSV files for organizing datasets, and GitHub to make our project publicly accessible. We also created a PowerPoint presentation to demonstrate our findings.

EarthScope aims to make Earth science data more accessible to students, researchers, and anyone interested in environmental changes. By presenting data visually, our project encourages users to explore climate trends and understand the importance of monitoring changes in Earth's environment.

Our approach focuses on making scientific information understandable through simple visualizations and accessible tools.
